observations: All four panels are the actual nativeCPU-MuJoCo400Hz episodes. PPO is PhysX-trained; CEM has native model prediction. No200Hz or alternate-training-origin substitution.
Fixed shared camera distance/orientation and root-relative translation are retained over the entire movie; no zoom, pose filtering or heading alignment hides instability.

The PPO-beta body tips after4s and remains fallen after4.5s. The original fall is visible through6.98s. Both CEM bodies stay upright in sampled full-horizon frames, but CEM-beta worldXY path deviates substantially.
Shared worldXY maps retain bodyheading and both wheel rolling-plane axes. The CEM+beta path follows the turn more closely in the core; the tail shows more overshoot than PPO+beta.
The final6.98s frame correctly reports XY error unavailable because the locked reference ends6.96s.
Four horizontal diagnostic plots show native XY, trackingerror, tilt and high-frequency motion. The lower PPO-beta HF during a fall is not labeled successful stability.
limitations: All350encoded frames and1400camera fits were checked numerically; visualinspection used selectedframes, not every encodedframe individually.
A50fps movie cannot resolve every400Hz contact/jitter event. Native spectra/contact statistics are required.
Wheel-force/count zero is not geometricflight or failure. Tilt/height/contact remain diagnostics, not added termination gates.
The figure does not establish exact PPO episode-return parity, optimizer-only causality, realtime feasibility or statistical superiority.
